Use this family whenever the response is a time-to-event outcome that may be right-censored — for example, time to failure, time to churn, or time to death/relapse in survival data — and the goal is to model how covariates shift the instantaneous risk of the event over time. Rather than a per-observation deviance and log-likelihood in the usual GLM sense, `CoxPH` maximizes the Cox partial likelihood via a custom `irls_update`, so the "response" `y` passed to `GAM.fit()` is the observed survival/censoring time, and the event indicator is supplied separately through `set_data()` (populated automatically by `GAM.fit()` from the column named by `status`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [status]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["event"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the column in the data dict containing the event indicator (`1` = event observed, `0` = right-censored). This column is looked up automatically from the data passed to `GAM.fit()`. [ties]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["breslow"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Tie-handling method for the partial likelihood when multiple observations share the same event time: `"breslow"` (default, simpler and faster) or `"efron"` (more accurate when ties are frequent). ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The hazard is modeled multiplicatively as $$ h(t \mid x) = h_0(t)\, e^{\eta(x)}, \qquad \eta(x) = X\beta, $$ where `h0(t)` is an unspecified baseline hazard and `eta` is the (possibly smooth) linear predictor, so `link` and `link_inverse` are both the identity. There is no closed-form variance function or unit deviance in the usual GLM sense; instead, model fitting maximizes the Cox partial log-likelihood, $$ \ell(\beta) = \sum_{i:\, \delta_i = 1} \left[ \eta_i - \log\!\left( \sum_{j \in R(t_i)} e^{\eta_j} \right) \right], $$ where $\delta_i$ is the event indicator and $R(t_i)$ is the risk set at time $t_i$ (those still under observation just before $t_i$). The overall "deviance" reported by `GAM.summary()` is $-2\ell(\beta)$. After fitting, `baseline_hazard()` and `survival_function()` expose the Breslow estimate of the cumulative baseline hazard and the implied survival curve. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a Cox proportional hazards GAM with a smooth effect of age on the hazard: ::: {#d77b8deb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 age = rng.uniform(40, 80, n) risk = np.exp(0.03 * (age - 60)) time = rng.exponential(1.0 / risk) censor_time = rng.exponential(2.0, n) observed_time = np.minimum(time, censor_time) event = (time <= censor_time).astype(float) data = {"time": observed_time, "age": age, "event": event} model = wk.GAM("time ~ s(age)", family=wk.CoxPH(status="event")) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: time ~ s(age) Family: CoxPH(ties='breslow') Inference: REML Observations: 300 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err z value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.0787 0.0731 1.077 0.2816 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(age) 1.00 2 23.749 6.966e-06 Total EDF: 2.00 Scale est: 1.000000 Deviance: 1824.6258 Null dev: 1848.4760 Dev. expl: 1.3% GCV score: 6.164024 AIC: 1828.63 BIC: 1836.04 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes} | {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature baseline_hazard() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the step-function estimate of $H_0(t) = \int_0^t h_0(u)\, du$ evaluated at each observed event time, [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L431-L456){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature deviance( y, mu, *, weights=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.deviance`. Since there is no saturated-model decomposition for the partial likelihood, this simply returns minus twice the partial log-likelihood evaluated at the current linear predictor, which `GAM.summary()` reports as the model deviance. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed survival/censoring times, shape `(n,)` (unused; retained for interface compatibility). [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values (`eta`), shape `(n,)`. [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Unused; `CoxPH` does not support prior weights. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : $-2\ell(\beta)$, the deviance. ::: ### [initialize()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Store the observed survival times and seed the linear predictor at zero. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L221-L243){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature initialize(y) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.initialize`. Records the sorted order of the observed times `y` (used throughout this file to walk risk sets from latest to earliest time) and starts P-IRLS from `eta = 0` for every observation, i.e. an initial hazard ratio of `exp(0) = 1` relative to the baseline. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed survival/censoring times, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of zeros with the same shape as `y`, used as the initial linear predictor. ::: ### [irls_update()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Newton step for the Cox partial likelihood, supplying custom working values. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L294-L355){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature irls_update( y, mu, eta, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.irls_update`. Rather than deriving the working response and weights from `link`, `link_derivative`, and `variance`, this computes the gradient $U(\eta)$ and diagonal Hessian $H(\eta)$ of the partial log-likelihood directly (via `_breslow_grad_hess` or `_efron_grad_hess`, depending on `ties`), and forms a Newton update $$ z = \eta + H(\eta)^{-1} U(\eta), \qquad W = \max(H(\eta), \epsilon), $$ so that a weighted least-squares fit of `z` on `W` reproduces one Newton-Raphson step on the partial log-likelihood. As a side effect, also refreshes the Breslow estimate of the cumulative baseline hazard via `_compute_baseline_hazard`, so that `baseline_hazard()` and `survival_function()` reflect the current fit. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed survival/censoring times, shape `(n,)` (unused directly; times were captured by `initialize`). [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current fitted values, identical to `eta` for this family, shape `(n,)`. [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple of NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `(z, W)`, the pseudo-response and diagonal working-weight vector, each shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called before `set_data()` has supplied the event indicator. ::: ### [link()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Identity link, $\eta = \mu$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L146-L163){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `CoxPH` does not model a conventional conditional mean; `mu` is instead identified with the linear predictor `eta`, so the link function is the identity. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values (treated as `mu`), shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The input array, unchanged. ::: ### [link_derivative()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function link_derivative(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Since `link` and `link_inverse` are both the identity, the derivative is constant `1` everywhere. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones with the same shape as `mu`. ::: ### [link_inverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Inverse identity link, $\mu = \eta$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L165-L181){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature link_inverse(eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Since `link` is the identity, its inverse is also the identity: the linear predictor is returned unchanged as `mu`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The input array, unchanged. ::: ### [log_likelihood()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Cox partial log-likelihood $\ell(\beta)$ at the current linear predictor. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L481-L509){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature log_likelihood( y, mu, scale, *, weights=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.log_likelihood`. Delegates to `_partial_log_likelihood`, which sums $\eta_i - \log \sum_{j \in R(t_i)} e^{\eta_j}$ over the observed events, using the Breslow or Efron tie-handling scheme selected by `ties`. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed survival/censoring times, shape `(n,)` (unused; retained for interface compatibility). [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values (`eta`), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; `CoxPH` has no free dispersion parameter (see `scale_known`). [weights]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Unused; `CoxPH` does not support prior weights. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The partial log-likelihood $\ell(\beta)$. ::: ### [set_data()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the event/censoring indicator from the fitting data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L120-L144){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature set_data(data) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.set_data`. Looks up the column named by the `status` constructor argument in `data` and stores it as the event indicator used by `irls_update`, `deviance`, and `log_likelihood` to identify which observations are actual events (`1`) versus right-censored (`0`). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, NDArray]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mapping of column names to arrays, as passed to `GAM.fit()`. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [KeyError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the status column is not present in `data`. ::: ### [simulate()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate survival times by inverting the fitted cumulative baseline hazard. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L523-L567){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature simulate( mu, scale, rng, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.simulate`. Draws $u \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0, 1)$ for each observation and solves for the target cumulative baseline hazard $H_0(t) = -\log(u) / e^{\eta}$ implied by the proportional-hazards model, then looks up the smallest fitted baseline event time whose cumulative baseline hazard (from `baseline_hazard()`) meets or exceeds that target. Observations whose target exceeds the largest observed cumulative hazard are assigned the last baseline time. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values (`eta`), shape `(n,)`. [scale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Unused; `CoxPH` has no free dispersion parameter. [rng]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [np.random.Generator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `numpy.random.Generator` instance used to draw the uniform variates. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Simulated survival times, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called before the model has been fitted (so no baseline hazard is available). ::: ### [survival_function()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fitted survival probability at the last event time. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L627-L657){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature survival_function(eta) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} $S(t \mid x) = \exp(-H_0(t)\, e^{\eta})$. Combines the given linear predictor with the final value of the Breslow cumulative baseline hazard (i.e. $H_0$ evaluated at the largest observed event time) to give the implied survival probability for each observation at that time, following the proportional-hazards relationship $S(t \mid x) = S_0(t)^{\exp(\eta)}$. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [eta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Linear predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fitted survival probabilities at the last observed event time, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [RuntimeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the model has not yet been fitted, so no baseline hazard exists. ::: ### [unit_deviance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Per-observation deviance placeholder (not decomposable for a partial likelihood). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L458-L479){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature unit_deviance( y, mu, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Implements the family-specific version of `Family.unit_deviance`. The Cox partial log-likelihood does not decompose into independent per-observation contributions the way an ordinary GLM deviance does, so this returns an array of ones purely to satisfy the `Family` interface; use `deviance` or `log_likelihood` for the actual fit statistics. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [y]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Observed survival/censoring times, shape `(n,)`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Current linear predictor values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones with the same shape as `y`. ::: ### [variance()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Variance function $V(\mu) = 1$. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/cox_ph.py#L201-L219){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature variance(mu) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `CoxPH` fits via the Cox partial likelihood rather than a GLM variance function, so this returns a constant `1` for every observation; it exists only to satisfy the `Family` interface and is not used by `irls_update`, which supplies its own working weights directly from the partial-likelihood Hessian. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Conditional mean values, shape `(n,)`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Array of ones with the same shape as `mu`. :::
